```ts
  26 | 
  27 | // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  28 | // Stale times
  29 | // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  30 | 
  31 | const STALE_TIMES = {
  32 |   /** Single visit row. */
  33 |   DETAIL: 60_000,
  34 |   /** Visit with measurements, diagnoses, prescriptions — heavier query. */
  35 |   WITH_DETAILS: 30_000,
  36 |   /** Patient's visit history. */
  37 |   PATIENT: 60_000,
  38 |   /** Clinic's visit list. */
  39 |   CLINIC: 60_000,
  40 |   /** Global "recent visits" list — used by the top-level visits page. */
  41 |   ALL: 60_000,
  42 | } as const;
  43 | 
  44 | // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  45 | // Query key factory
  46 | // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  47 | 
  48 | type VisitSearch = z.infer<typeof visitSearchSchema>;
  49 | 
  50 | export const visitKeys = {
  51 |   all: () => ["visit"] as const,
  52 | 
  53 |   /** Global "recent visits" list (clinic-scoped). */
  54 |   recent: (clinicId: string) => ["visit", "recent", clinicId] as const,
  55 | 
  56 |   /** A clinic's visit list with the search/filter applied. */
  57 |   list: (clinicId: string, search: VisitSearch | undefined) =>
  58 |     [
  59 |       "visit",
  60 |       "list",
  61 |       clinicId,
  62 |       search?.page ?? 1,
  63 |       search?.pageSize ?? 25,
  64 |       search?.sort ?? "visitedAt",
  65 |       search?.dir ?? "desc",
  66 |       search?.doctorId ?? "any",
  67 |       search?.patientId ?? "any",
  68 |     ] as const,
  69 | 
  70 |   /** Per-patient subtree. */
  71 |   patient: (patientId: string) => ["visit", "patient", patientId] as const,
  72 | 
  73 |   /** Single visit row. */
  74 |   detail: (visitId: string) => ["visit", "detail", visitId] as const,
  75 | 
  76 |   /** Visit + measurements + diagnoses + prescriptions. */
  77 |   withDetails: (visitId: string) => ["visit", "detail", visitId, "details"] as const,
  78 | } as const;
  79 | 
  80 | // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  81 | // Query options
  82 | // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  83 | 
  84 | export function visitQuery(visitId: string) {
  85 |   return queryOptions({
  86 |     queryKey: visitKeys.detail(visitId),
  87 |     queryFn: () => fetchVisitById({ data: { visitId } }),
  88 |     staleTime: STALE_TIMES.DETAIL,
  89 |   });
  90 | }
  91 | 
  92 | export function visitWithDetailsQuery(visitId: string) {
  93 |   return queryOptions({
  94 |     queryKey: visitKeys.withDetails(visitId),
  95 |     queryFn: () => fetchVisitWithDetails({ data: { visitId } }),
  96 |     staleTime: STALE_TIMES.WITH_DETAILS,
  97 |   });
  98 | }
  99 | 
 100 | export function patientVisitsQuery(patientId: string) {
 101 |   return queryOptions({
 102 |     queryKey: visitKeys.patient(patientId),
 103 |     queryFn: () => fetchVisitsForPatient({ data: { patientId } }),
 104 |     staleTime: STALE_TIMES.PATIENT,
 105 |   });
 106 | }
 107 | 
 108 | export function clinicVisitsQuery(clinicId: string, search?: VisitSearch) {
 109 |   return queryOptions({
 110 |     queryKey: visitKeys.list(clinicId, search),
 111 |     queryFn: () => fetchVisitsForClinic({ data: { clinicId, search } }),
 112 |     staleTime: STALE_TIMES.CLINIC,
 113 |   });
 114 | }
 115 | 
 116 | export function recentVisitsQuery(clinicId: string) {
 117 |   return queryOptions({
 118 |     queryKey: visitKeys.recent(clinicId),
 119 |     queryFn: () => fetchAllVisits({ data: { clinicId } }),
 120 |     staleTime: STALE_TIMES.ALL,
 121 |   });
 122 | }
 123 | 
 124 | // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 125 | // Invalidation
 126 | // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 127 | 
 128 | /**
 129 |  * Call after a visit mutation succeeds.
 130 |  *
 131 |  * A visit write touches:
 132 |  *   1. The visit's own detail entries (`visitKeys.detail(visitId)`).
 133 |  *   2. The patient's visit history (`visitKeys.patient(patientId)`).
 134 |  *   3. The clinic's visit list and recent list.
 135 |  *   4. The patient's growth series — visits feed measurements, and a
 136 |  *      measurement is always attached to a visit.
 137 |  *
 138 |  * `createVisitFn` doesn't know the new visit's id yet, so callers may omit
 139 |  * `visitId` when invalidating after a create.
 140 |  */
 141 | export function invalidateAfterVisitMutation(
 142 |   queryClient: {
 143 |     invalidateQueries: (opts: { queryKey: readonly unknown[] }) => unknown;
 144 |   },
 145 |   args: {
 146 |     clinicId: string;
 147 |     patientId: string;
 148 |     visitId?: string;
 149 |   },
 150 | ): Promise<unknown> {
 151 |   const promises: Array<unknown> = [
 152 |     queryClient.invalidateQueries({
 153 |       queryKey: visitKeys.patient(args.patientId),
 154 |     }),
 155 |     queryClient.invalidateQueries({
 156 |       queryKey: visitKeys.list(args.clinicId, undefined),
 157 |     }),
 158 |     queryClient.invalidateQueries({
 159 |       queryKey: visitKeys.recent(args.clinicId),
 160 |     }),
 161 |     // Visits create measurements, so growth caches need to refetch.
 162 |     queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ["series", args.patientId] }),
 163 |     queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ["latest", args.patientId] }),
 164 |   ];
 165 | 
 166 |   if (args.visitId) {
 167 |     // `detail` is the parent of `withDetails`, so one invalidation
 168 |     // drops both the row query and the composed query.
 169 |     promises.push(
 170 |       queryClient.invalidateQueries({
 171 |         queryKey: visitKeys.detail(args.visitId),
 172 |       }),
 173 |     );
 174 |   }
 175 | 
 176 |   return Promise.all(promises);
 177 | }
 178 | 
 179 | export function useCreateVisitMutation() {
 180 |   const queryClient = useQueryClient();
 181 |   const createVisit = useServerFn(createVisitFn);
 182 | 
 183 |   return useMutation({
 184 |     mutationKey: ["visit", "create"],
 185 |     mutationFn: (input: Parameters<typeof createVisit>[0]["data"]) => createVisit({ data: input }),
 186 |     onSuccess: async (visit, input) => {
 187 |       await invalidateAfterVisitMutation(queryClient, {
 188 |         clinicId: input.clinicId,
 189 |         patientId: input.patientId,
 190 |         visitId: visit.id,
 191 |       });
 192 |     },
 193 |   });
 194 | }
 195 | 
 196 | export function useDeleteVisitMutation() {
 197 |   const queryClient = useQueryClient();
 198 |   const deleteVisit = useServerFn(deleteVisitFn);
 199 | 
 200 |   return useMutation({
 201 |     mutationKey: ["visit", "delete"],
 202 |     mutationFn: (input: { visitId: string; clinicId: string; patientId: string }) =>
 203 |       deleteVisit({ data: { visitId: input.visitId } }),
 204 |     onSuccess: async (_result, input) => {
 205 |       await invalidateAfterVisitMutation(queryClient, input);
 206 |     },
 207 |   });
 208 | }
```

`hooks/use-callback-ref.tsx`:

```tsx
   1 | import * as React from "react";
   2 | 
   3 | /**
   4 |  * @see https://github.com/radix-ui/primitives/blob/main/packages/react/use-callback-ref/src/useCallbackRef.tsx
   5 |  */
   6 | 
   7 | /**
   8 |  * A custom hook that converts a callback to a ref to avoid triggering re-renders when passed as a
   9 |  * prop or avoid re-executing effects when passed as a dependency
  10 |  */
  11 | // `never[]` (not `unknown[]`) is the sound way to constrain "any function":
  12 | // `never` is assignable to every type, so specific-typed callbacks such as
  13 | // `(state: T) => void` satisfy the constraint. With `unknown[]` the parameter
  14 | // is contravariant and `(state: T) => void` is rejected, since `unknown` is
  15 | // not assignable to `T`.
  16 | function useCallbackRef<T extends (...args: never[]) => unknown>(callback: T | undefined): T {
  17 |   const callbackRef = React.useRef(callback);
  18 | 
  19 |   // Intentionally no dependency array - we want to update the ref on every render
  20 |   // so the latest callback is always available. This is safe because we're only
  21 |   // updating a ref, not triggering side effects.
  22 |   React.useEffect(() => {
  23 |     callbackRef.current = callback;
  24 |   });
  25 | 
  26 |   // https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/19240
  27 |   return React.useMemo(() => ((...args: never[]) => callbackRef.current?.(...args)) as T, []);
  28 | }
  29 | 
  30 | export { useCallbackRef };
```

`hooks/use-controllable-state.tsx`:

```tsx
   1 | import React from "react";
   2 | 
   3 | import { useCallbackRef } from "./use-callback-ref";
   4 | 
   5 | /**
   6 |  * @see https://github.com/radix-ui/primitives/blob/main/packages/react/use-controllable-state/src/useControllableState.tsx
   7 |  */
   8 | 
   9 | interface UseControllableStateParams<T> {
  10 |   prop?: T | undefined;
  11 |   defaultProp?: T | undefined;
  12 |   onChange?: (state: T) => void;
  13 | }
  14 | 
  15 | type SetStateFn<T> = (prevState?: T) => T;
  16 | 
  17 | function useControllableState<T>({ prop, defaultProp, onChange }: UseControllableStateParams<T>) {
  18 |   const [uncontrolledProp, setUncontrolledProp] = useUncontrolledState({
  19 |     defaultProp,
  20 |     onChange,
  21 |   });
  22 |   const isControlled = prop !== undefined;
  23 |   const value = isControlled ? prop : uncontrolledProp;
  24 |   const handleChange = useCallbackRef(onChange);
  25 | 
  26 |   const setValue: React.Dispatch<React.SetStateAction<T | undefined>> = React.useCallback(
  27 |     (nextValue) => {
  28 |       if (isControlled) {
  29 |         const setter = nextValue as SetStateFn<T>;
  30 |         const resolvedValue = typeof nextValue === "function" ? setter(prop) : nextValue;
  31 |         if (resolvedValue !== prop) {
  32 |           handleChange(resolvedValue as T);
  33 |         }
  34 |       } else {
  35 |         setUncontrolledProp(nextValue);
  36 |       }
  37 |     },
  38 |     [isControlled, prop, setUncontrolledProp, handleChange],
  39 |   );
  40 | 
  41 |   return [value, setValue] as const;
  42 | }
  43 | 
  44 | function useUncontrolledState<T>({
  45 |   defaultProp,
  46 |   onChange,
  47 | }: {
  48 |   defaultProp?: T | undefined;
  49 |   onChange?: ((state: T) => void) | undefined;
  50 | }) {
  51 |   const [value, setValue] = React.useState<T | undefined>(defaultProp);
  52 |   const prevValueRef = React.useRef(value);
  53 |   const handleChange = useCallbackRef(onChange);
  54 | 
  55 |   React.useEffect(() => {
  56 |     if (prevValueRef.current !== value) {
  57 |       handleChange(value as T);
  58 |       prevValueRef.current = value;
  59 |     }
  60 |   }, [value, handleChange]);
  61 | 
  62 |   return [value, setValue] as const;
  63 | }
  64 | 
  65 | export { useControllableState };
```

`hooks/use-copy-to-clipboard.tsx`:

```tsx
   1 | import * as React from "react";
   2 | 
   3 | export interface UseCopyToClipboardProps {
   4 |   timeout?: number;
   5 | }
   6 | 
   7 | export function useCopyToClipboard({ timeout = 2000 }: UseCopyToClipboardProps = {}) {
   8 |   const [isCopied, setIsCopied] = React.useState<boolean>(false);
   9 | 
  10 |   const timeoutRef = React.useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null>(null);
  11 | 
  12 |   React.useEffect(
  13 |     () => () => {
  14 |       if (timeoutRef.current !== null) {
  15 |         clearTimeout(timeoutRef.current);
  16 |       }
  17 |     },
  18 |     [],
  19 |   );
  20 | 
  21 |   const copyToClipboard = React.useCallback(
  22 |     async (value: string): Promise<boolean> => {
  23 |       if (!value) {
  24 |         return false;
  25 |       }
  26 | 
  27 |       // `navigator.clipboard` is absent on non-secure origins
  28 |       // (plain HTTP) and in older browsers. The DOM lib types it as
  29 |       // Non-optional, so we widen it here — the runtime check is
  30 |       // Real, only the type needs correcting.
  31 |       const { clipboard } = globalThis.navigator as Navigator & {
  32 |         clipboard?: Clipboard;
  33 |       };
  34 | 
  35 |       try {
  36 |         await clipboard.writeText(value);
  37 |       } catch {
  38 |         // NotAllowedError when the document isn't focused, or the
  39 |         // Permission prompt is denied. Treat as failure, not a crash.
  40 |         return false;
  41 |       }
  42 | 
  43 |       setIsCopied(true);
  44 |       if (timeoutRef.current !== null) {
  45 |         clearTimeout(timeoutRef.current);
  46 |       }
  47 |       timeoutRef.current = setTimeout(() => {
  48 |         setIsCopied(false);
  49 |         timeoutRef.current = null;
  50 |       }, timeout);
  51 | 
  52 |       return true;
  53 |     },
  54 |     [timeout],
  55 |   );
  56 | 
  57 |   return { copyToClipboard, isCopied };
  58 | }
```

```ts
   1 | import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
   2 | 
   3 | export function useDebounce<T>(value: T, delay?: number): T {
   4 |   const [debouncedValue, setDebouncedValue] = useState<T>(value);
   5 | 
   6 |   useEffect(() => {
   7 |     const timer = setTimeout(() => {
   8 |       setDebouncedValue(value);
   9 |     }, delay || 500);
  10 | 
  11 |     return () => {
  12 |       clearTimeout(timer);
  13 |     };
  14 |   }, [value, delay]);
  15 | 
  16 |   return debouncedValue;
  17 | }
```

`hooks/use-debounced-callback.ts`:

```ts
   1 | import * as React from "react";
   2 | 
   3 | import { useCallbackRef } from "./use-callback-ref";
   4 | 
   5 | export function useDebouncedCallback<T extends (...args: unknown[]) => unknown>(
   6 |   callback: T,
   7 |   delay: number,
   8 | ) {
   9 |   const handleCallback = useCallbackRef(callback);
  10 |   const debounceTimerRef = React.useRef<ReturnType<typeof globalThis.setTimeout> | null>(null);
  11 |   React.useEffect(
  12 |     () => () => {
  13 |       if (debounceTimerRef.current !== null) {
  14 |         globalThis.clearTimeout(debounceTimerRef.current);
  15 |       }
  16 |     },
  17 |     [],
  18 |   );
  19 | 
  20 |   const setValue = React.useCallback(
  21 |     (...args: Parameters<T>) => {
  22 |       if (debounceTimerRef.current !== null) {
  23 |         globalThis.clearTimeout(debounceTimerRef.current);
  24 |       }
  25 |       debounceTimerRef.current = globalThis.setTimeout(() => handleCallback(...args), delay);
  26 |     },
  27 |     [handleCallback, delay],
  28 |   );
  29 | 
  30 |   return setValue;
  31 | }
```

`hooks/use-highlighted-code.ts`:

```ts
   1 | import * as React from "react";
   2 | 
   3 | import { loadHighlighter } from "#/lib/highlighter";
   4 | 
   5 | export function useHighlightedCode(value: string, language: string) {
   6 |   // A trailing newline would render as an extra empty line.
   7 |   const code = value.endsWith("\n") ? value.slice(0, -1) : value;
   8 |   const [loaded, setLoaded] = React.useState<{
   9 |     language: string;
  10 |     highlighter: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof loadHighlighter>>;
  11 |   } | null>(null);
  12 |   const highlighter = loaded?.language === language ? loaded.highlighter : null;
  13 | 
  14 |   React.useEffect(() => {
  15 |     let cancelled = false;
  16 | 
  17 |     loadHighlighter(language)
  18 |       .then((next) => {
  19 |         if (!cancelled) {
  20 |           setLoaded({ language, highlighter: next });
  21 |         }
  22 |       })
  23 |       .catch(() => {});
  24 | 
  25 |     return () => {
  26 |       cancelled = true;
  27 |     };
  28 |   }, [language]);
  29 | 
  30 |   // The complete lines, highlighted. While the code streams, only the new
  31 |   // lines are tokenized, starting from the grammar state of the last one.
  32 |   const [done, setDone] = React.useState<{
  33 |     highlighter: typeof highlighter;
  34 |     text: string;
  35 |     lines: React.ReactNode[];
  36 |     state?: Parameters<NonNullable<typeof highlighter>["highlight"]>[1];
  37 |   }>({ highlighter: null, text: "", lines: [] });
  38 | 
  39 |   let next = done;
  40 | 
  41 |   if (next.highlighter !== highlighter || !code.startsWith(next.text)) {
  42 |     next = { highlighter, text: "", lines: [] };
  43 |   }
  44 | 
  45 |   const end = code.lastIndexOf("\n") + 1;
  46 | 
  47 |   if (highlighter && end > next.text.length) {
  48 |     const result = highlighter.highlight(code.slice(next.text.length, end - 1), next.state);
  49 | 
  50 |     next = {
  51 |       highlighter,
  52 |       text: code.slice(0, end),
  53 |       lines: [...next.lines, ...result.lines],
  54 |       state: result.state,
  55 |     };
  56 |   }
  57 | 
  58 |   if (next !== done) {
  59 |     setDone(next);
  60 |   }
  61 | 
  62 |   // The last line is still being written, so it is tokenized on every render.
  63 |   const tail = code.slice(end);
  64 | 
  65 |   return React.useMemo(() => {
  66 |     if (!highlighter) {
  67 |       return code.split("\n");
  68 |     }
  69 | 
  70 |     return [...next.lines, highlighter.highlight(tail, next.state).lines[0]];
  71 |   }, [code, highlighter, next, tail]);
  72 | }
```

`hooks/use-keyboard-shortcuts.tsx`:

```tsx
   1 | import { useEffect } from "react";
   2 | 
   3 | export interface KeyCombination {
   4 |   keys: {
   5 |     ctrlKey?: boolean;
   6 |     metaKey?: boolean;
   7 |     shiftKey?: boolean;
   8 |     altKey?: boolean;
   9 |   };
  10 |   key: string;
  11 |   handler: (event: KeyboardEvent) => void;
  12 |   /** Whether to automatically call event.preventDefault() when the shortcut matches. Defaults to true. */
  13 |   preventDefault?: boolean;
  14 | }
  15 | 
  16 | export function useKeyboardShortcuts(combinations: KeyCombination[]) {
  17 |   useEffect(() => {
  18 |     const handleKeyDown = (event: KeyboardEvent) => {
  19 |       combinations.forEach((combo) => {
  20 |         const {
  21 |           keys: { ctrlKey, metaKey, shiftKey, altKey },
  22 |           key,
  23 |           handler,
  24 |         } = combo;
  25 |         const isMatch =
  26 |           (ctrlKey === undefined || event.ctrlKey === ctrlKey) &&
  27 |           (metaKey === undefined || event.metaKey === metaKey) &&
  28 |           (shiftKey === undefined || event.shiftKey === shiftKey) &&
  29 |           (altKey === undefined || event.altKey === altKey) &&
  30 |           event.key.toLowerCase() === key.toLowerCase();
  31 | 
  32 |         if (isMatch) {
  33 |           if (combo.preventDefault !== false) {
  34 |             event.preventDefault();
  35 |           }
  36 |           handler(event);
  37 |         }
  38 |       });
  39 |     };
  40 | 
  41 |     globalThis.addEventListener("keydown", handleKeyDown);
  42 | 
  43 |     // Cleanup event listener on unmount
  44 |     return () => {
  45 |       globalThis.removeEventListener("keydown", handleKeyDown);
  46 |     };
  47 |   }, [combinations]);
  48 | }
```

```ts
   1 | import { useCallback, useState } from "react";
   2 | 
   3 | // Open state for a dialog whose code loads on first use. `used` stays true after closing,
   4 | // so the dialog stays mounted and its exit animation can run.
   5 | export function useLazyDialog() {
   6 |   const [open, setOpenState] = useState(false);
   7 |   const [used, setUsed] = useState(false);
   8 | 
   9 |   const setOpen = useCallback((next: React.SetStateAction<boolean>) => {
  10 |     setUsed(true);
  11 |     setOpenState(next);
  12 |   }, []);
  13 | 
  14 |   // Called when the dialog's chunk fails to load, so the shell carries on without it.
  15 |   const reset = useCallback(() => {
  16 |     setUsed(false);
  17 |     setOpenState(false);
  18 |   }, []);
  19 | 
  20 |   return { open, used, setOpen, reset };
  21 | }
```

```ts
   1 | import * as React from "react";

   3 | const MOBILE_BREAKPOINT = 768;
   4 | 
   5 | export function useIsMobile() {
   6 |   const [isMobile, setIsMobile] = React.useState<boolean>(() => {
   7 |     if (typeof window === "undefined" || typeof window.matchMedia !== "function") {
   8 |       return false;
   9 |     }
  10 |     return window.matchMedia(`(max-width: ${MOBILE_BREAKPOINT - 1}px)`).matches;
  11 |   });
  12 | 
  13 |   React.useEffect(() => {
  14 |     const mql = window.matchMedia(`(max-width: ${MOBILE_BREAKPOINT - 1}px)`);
  15 |     const onChange = () => {
  16 |       setIsMobile(mql.matches);
  17 |     };
  18 |     mql.addEventListener("change", onChange);
  19 |     return () => mql.removeEventListener("change", onChange);
  20 |   }, []);
  21 | 
  22 |   return isMobile;
  23 | }
```

```ts
   1 | import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
   2 | 
   3 | export function useScroll(downThreshold: number, upThreshold?: number) {
   4 |   const [scrolled, setScrolled] = useState(false);
   5 |   const scrollUpThreshold = upThreshold ?? downThreshold / 2;
   6 | 
   7 |   useEffect(() => {
   8 |     const handleScroll = () => {
   9 |       const y = window.scrollY;
  10 |       // Hysteresis: different thresholds for up/down to prevent flickering
  11 |       setScrolled((prev) => {
  12 |         if (prev) {
  13 |           // Currently scrolled - only unscroll when below lower threshold
  14 |           return y > scrollUpThreshold;
  15 |         }
  16 |         // Currently not scrolled - only scroll when above higher threshold
  17 |         return y > downThreshold;
  18 |       });
  19 |     };
  20 | 
  21 |     window.addEventListener("scroll", handleScroll, { passive: true });
  22 |     handleScroll();
  23 |     return () => {
  24 |       window.removeEventListener("scroll", handleScroll);
  25 |     };
  26 |   }, [downThreshold, scrollUpThreshold]);
  27 | 
  28 |   return scrolled;
  29 | }
```

`integrations/tanstack-query/query-client.ts`:

```ts
   1 | // src/integrations/tanstack-query/query-client.ts
   2 | //
   3 | // Do NOT export a top-level `queryClient` constant alongside
   4 | // `getQueryClient()`. The constant would be a *different* instance from
   5 | // what `getQueryClient()` returns on the browser, which means:
   6 | //   - `queryClient.invalidateQueries(...)` against one instance does not
   7 | //     reach components subscribed to the other;
   8 | //   - SSR and the client see different caches.
   9 | // Only export the factory + the singleton accessor. If existing code
  10 | // imports `{ queryClient }`, replace it with:
  11 | //   - `useQueryClient()` inside components / hooks;
  12 | //   - `getQueryClient()` inside event handlers or non-component code.
  13 | // See: rg "from ['\"].*query-client['\"]" src/
  14 | 
  15 | import { MutationCache, QueryCache, QueryClient } from "@tanstack/react-query";
  16 | 
  17 | import { toast } from "#/components/ui/toast.tsx";
  18 | 
  19 | /**
  20 |  * Report an error to the browser's global error reporter.
  21 |  *
  22 |  * `globalThis.reportError` (per the HTML spec) is `(error: any) => void`
  23 |  * and its argument should be an `Error` — not an arbitrary object. We
  24 |  * attach the metadata as an own property on the error so reporters that
  25 |  * forward `error.metadata` (Sentry, etc.) still get it.
  26 |  */
  27 | function reportQueryError(message: string, metadata: Record<string, unknown>) {
  28 |   const err = new Error(message);
  29 |   Object.assign(err, { metadata });
  30 | 
  31 |   if (typeof globalThis.reportError === "function") {
  32 |     globalThis.reportError(err);
  33 |     return;
  34 |   }
  35 | 
  36 |   console.warn(message, metadata);
  37 | }
  38 | 
  39 | /**
  40 |  * Minimum time (ms) between two global query-error toasts.
  41 |  *
  42 |  * Without this, a single network hiccup producing N failing queries
  43 |  * produces N identical toasts, and on flaky Wi-Fi the user sees a toast
  44 |  * storm while the page already renders its own `SectionState` error UI.
  45 |  * The window is arbitrary — 3s lets a genuinely new failure through
  46 |  * while coalescing bursts.
  47 |  */
  48 | const TOAST_WINDOW_MS = 3000;
  49 | let lastQueryErrorToastAt = 0;
  50 | 
  51 | export function createQueryClient(): QueryClient {
  52 |   return new QueryClient({
  53 |     defaultOptions: {
  54 |       mutations: { retry: false },
  55 |       queries: {
  56 |         gcTime: 5 * 60 * 1000, // 5 minutes
  57 |         refetchOnReconnect: true,
  58 |         refetchOnWindowFocus: false, // Clinic app: focus events are constant
  59 |         retry: (failureCount, error) => {
  60 |           const { status } = error as { status?: unknown };
  61 |           // Authentication/authorization failures won't recover by
  62 |           // retrying the same request with the same session.
  63 |           if (status === 401 || status === 403) {
  64 |             return false;
  65 |           }
  66 |           return failureCount < 3;
  67 |         },
  68 |         staleTime: 30 * 1000, // 30 seconds
  69 |       },
  70 |     },
  71 | 
  72 |     mutationCache: new MutationCache({
  73 |       onError: (error, mutation) => {
  74 |         reportQueryError("[Mutation Error]", {
  75 |           error,
  76 |           mutationKey: (mutation as { options: { mutationKey?: unknown } }).options.mutationKey,
  77 |         });
  78 |       },
  79 |     }),
  80 | 
  81 |     queryCache: new QueryCache({
  82 |       onError: (error, _query) => {
  83 |         const { status } = error as { status?: unknown };
  84 |         if (status === 401 || status === 403) {
  85 |           return;
  86 |         }
  87 | 
  88 |         const now = Date.now();
  89 |         if (now - lastQueryErrorToastAt < TOAST_WINDOW_MS) return;
  90 |         lastQueryErrorToastAt = now;
  91 | 
  92 |         toast.add({
  93 |           description: error instanceof Error ? error.message : "Request failed",
  94 |           title: "Error",
  95 |           type: "error",
  96 |         });
  97 |       },
  98 |     }),
  99 |   });
 100 | }
 101 | 
 102 | /**
 103 |  * The QueryClient for the current environment.
 104 |  *
 105 |  * - **Server:** a fresh instance on every call, so concurrent SSR
 106 |  *   requests never leak cache entries into each other (per-request
 107 |  *   isolation — the same property `getClinicStore()` maintains).
 108 |  * - **Browser:** one lazily-created singleton, shared by every component,
 109 |  *   hook, and event handler. This is what makes `invalidateQueries`
 110 |  *   reach the mounted tree.
 111 |  */
 112 | let browserClient: QueryClient | undefined;
 113 | 
 114 | export function getQueryClient(): QueryClient {
 115 |   if (typeof window === "undefined") {
 116 |     return createQueryClient();
 117 |   }
 118 |   browserClient ??= createQueryClient();
 119 |   return browserClient;
 120 | }
```

`lib/auth/clinic-middleware.ts`:

```ts
   1 | import { createMiddleware } from "@tanstack/react-start";
   2 | import { setResponseStatus } from "@tanstack/react-start/server";
   3 | 
   4 | import { db, eq } from "@/db";
   5 | import { appointments, patients, visits } from "@/db/schema";
   6 | 
   7 | import { freshAuthMiddleware } from "./middleware";
   8 | 
   9 | /**
  10 |  * Extracts the clinic id from a payload. Server functions must pass a
  11 |  * `clinicId`, `patientId`, `visitId`, or `appointmentId`; this middleware
  12 |  * resolves all four down to a clinic id.
  13 |  */
  14 | async function resolveClinicId(data: unknown): Promise<string | null> {
  15 |   if (!data || typeof data !== "object") return null;
  16 |   const d = data as Record<string, unknown>;
  17 | 
  18 |   if (typeof d.clinicId === "string") return d.clinicId;
  19 | 
  20 |   if (typeof d.patientId === "string") {
  21 |     const [row] = await db
  22 |       .select({ clinicId: patients.clinicId })
  23 |       .from(patients)
  24 |       .where(eq(patients.id, d.patientId))
  25 |       .limit(1);
  26 |     return row?.clinicId ?? null;
  27 |   }
  28 | 
  29 |   if (typeof d.visitId === "string") {
  30 |     const [row] = await db
  31 |       .select({ clinicId: visits.clinicId })
  32 |       .from(visits)
  33 |       .where(eq(visits.id, d.visitId))
  34 |       .limit(1);
  35 |     return row?.clinicId ?? null;
  36 |   }
  37 | 
  38 |   if (typeof d.appointmentId === "string") {
  39 |     const [row] = await db
  40 |       .select({ clinicId: appointments.clinicId })
  41 |       .from(appointments)
  42 |       .where(eq(appointments.id, d.appointmentId))
  43 |       .limit(1);
  44 |     return row?.clinicId ?? null;
  45 |   }
  46 | 
  47 |   // Mutations that accept a `patch` or `rows` array recurse.
  48 |   if (d.patch) return resolveClinicId(d.patch);
  49 |   if (Array.isArray(d.rows)) {
  50 |     for (const row of d.rows) {
  51 |       const id = await resolveClinicId(row);
  52 |       if (id) return id;
  53 |     }
  54 |   }
  55 | 
  56 |   return null;
  57 | }
  58 | 
  59 | /**
  60 |  * Requires the caller to be authenticated AND to belong to the same clinic
  61 |  * as the entity they're touching. Admins bypass the clinic check.
  62 |  */
  63 | export const clinicAccessMiddleware = createMiddleware({ type: "function" }) // ← Add this
  64 |   .middleware([freshAuthMiddleware])
  65 |   .server(async ({ next, data, context }) => {
  66 |     const clinicId = await resolveClinicId(data);
  67 |     if (!clinicId) {
  68 |       setResponseStatus(400);
  69 |       throw new Error("Cannot resolve a clinic from the request payload");
  70 |     }
  71 |     if (context.user.role !== "admin" && context.user.clinicId !== clinicId) {
  72 |       setResponseStatus(403);
  73 |       throw new Error("Forbidden: cross-clinic access denied");
  74 |     }
  75 |     return next({ context: { clinicId } });
  76 |   });
```

  65 | import { createMiddleware } from "@tanstack/react-start";

  68 | import { db, eq } from "@/db";
  69 | import { appointments, patients, visits } from "@/db/schema";
  70 | 
  71 | import { freshAuthMiddleware } from "./middleware";
  72 | 
  73 | /**
  74 |  * Extracts the clinic id from a payload. Server functions must pass a
  75 |  * `clinicId`, `patientId`, `visitId`, or `appointmentId`; this middleware
  76 |  * resolves all four down to a clinic id.
  77 |  */
  78 | async function resolveClinicId(data: unknown): Promise<string | null> {
  79 | 	if (!data || typeof data !== "object") return null;
  80 | 	const d = data as Record<string, unknown>;
  81 | 
  82 | 	if (typeof d.clinicId === "string") return d.clinicId;
  83 | 
  84 | 	if (typeof d.patientId === "string") {
  85 | 		const [row] = await db
  86 | 			.select({ clinicId: patients.clinicId })
  87 | 			.from(patients)
  88 | 			.where(eq(patients.id, d.patientId))
  89 | 			.limit(1);
  90 | 		return row?.clinicId ?? null;
  91 | 	}
  92 | 
  93 | 	if (typeof d.visitId === "string") {
  94 | 		const [row] = await db
  95 | 			.select({ clinicId: visits.clinicId })
  96 | 			.from(visits)
  97 | 			.where(eq(visits.id, d.visitId))
  98 | 			.limit(1);
  99 | 		return row?.clinicId ?? null;
 100 | 	}
 101 | 
 102 | 	if (typeof d.appointmentId === "string") {
 103 | 		const [row] = await db
 104 | 			.select({ clinicId: appointments.clinicId })
 105 | 			.from(appointments)
 106 | 			.where(eq(appointments.id, d.appointmentId))
 107 | 			.limit(1);
 108 | 		return row?.clinicId ?? null;
 109 | 	}
 110 | 
 111 | 	// Mutations that accept a `patch` or `rows` array recurse.
 112 | 	if (d.patch) return resolveClinicId(d.patch);
 113 | 	if (Array.isArray(d.rows)) {
 114 | 		for (const row of d.rows) {
 115 | 			const id = await resolveClinicId(row);
 116 | 			if (id) return id;
 117 | 		}
 118 | 	}
 119 | 
 120 | 	return null;
 121 | }
 122 | 
 123 | /**
 124 |  * Requires the caller to be authenticated AND to belong to the same clinic
 125 |  * as the entity they're touching. Admins bypass the clinic check.
 126 |  */
 127 | export const clinicAccessMiddleware = createMiddleware({ type: "function" }) // ← Add this
 128 | 	.middleware([freshAuthMiddleware])
 129 | 	.server(async ({ next, data, context }) => {
 130 | 		const clinicId = await resolveClinicId(data);
 131 | 		if (!clinicId) {
 132 | 			setResponseStatus(400);
 133 | 			throw new Error("Cannot resolve a clinic from the request payload");
 134 | 		}
 135 | 		if (context.user.role !== "admin" && context.user.clinicId !== clinicId) {
 136 | 			setResponseStatus(403);
 137 | 			throw new Error("Forbidden: cross-clinic access denied");
 138 | 		}
 139 | 		return next({ context: { clinicId } });
 140 | 	});

 605 |  *
 606 |  * Auth cookie cache is disabled, and fresh user session is always fetched from database.
 607 |  * This is recommended for sensitive/destructive operations and mutations that require the freshest auth state, e.g. to prevent a user from performing an action after their session has expired or been revoked.
 608 |  *
 609 |  * @see https://better-auth.com/docs/concepts/session-management#cookie-cache
 610 |  */
 611 | export const freshAuthMiddleware = createMiddleware().server(
 612 | 	async ({ next }) => {
 613 | 		const user = await _getUser({
 614 | 			// ensure session is fresh
 615 | 			// https://better-auth.com/docs/concepts/session-management#cookie-cache
 616 | 			disableCookieCache: true
 617 | 		});
 618 | 
 619 | 		if (!user) {
 620 | 			setResponseStatus(401);
 621 | 			throw new Error("Unauthorized");
 622 | 		}
 623 | 
 624 | 		return next({ context: { user } });
 625 | 	}
 626 | );
 627 |

1113 | import { z } from "zod";
1114 | 
1115 | /**
1116 |  * Canonical role vocabulary.
1117 |  *
1118 |  * ⚠️ This is the single source of truth for user roles. `schemas/enums.ts`
1119 |  * re-exports `USER_ROLES` and `userRoleSchema` from here — do NOT define a
1120 |  * second list there. Two enums with the same members but different order
1121 |  * are structurally identical but nominally distinct under TypeScript, and
1122 |  * `UserRole`/`Role` would stop being assignable to each other.
1123 |  */
1124 | export const USER_ROLES = ["admin", "doctor", "patient", "staff"] as const;
1125 | 
1126 | export const userRoleSchema = z.enum(USER_ROLES);
1127 | export type Role = z.infer<typeof userRoleSchema>;
1128 | 
1129 | export const rolesMapSchema = z.record(z.string(), userRoleSchema);
1130 | export type RolesMap = z.infer<typeof rolesMapSchema>;
1131 | 
1132 | export const ROLES_MAP = {
1133 | 	ADMIN: "admin",
1134 | 	DOCTOR: "doctor",
1135 | 	PATIENT: "patient",
1136 | 	STAFF: "staff"
1137 | } as const satisfies RolesMap;

1147 | 
1148 | // Utils.ts (dev-only branch, keep the warn in prod path)
1149 | export function sendPasswordResetEmail(email: string, url: string): void {
1150 | 	if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production") {
1151 | 		// Dev has no mailer — surface the reset URL so the flow is testable.
1152 | 		console.warn({
1153 | 			email,
1154 | 			level: "info",
1155 | 			msg: "Password reset URL (dev)",
1156 | 			url
1157 | 		});
1158 | 		return;

1164 | 	});

1166 | interface CachedRole {
1167 | 	role: Role;
1168 | 	banned: boolean;
1169 | 	banReason: string | null;
1170 | 	clinicId: string | null;
1171 | 	banExpires: Date | null;
1172 | 	expiresAt: number;
1173 | }
1174 | 
1175 | const ROLE_CACHE_TTL_MS = 60_000;
1176 | const roleCache = new Map<string, CachedRole>();
1177 | 
1178 | export function getCachedRole(userId: string) {
1179 | 	const entry = roleCache.get(userId);
1180 | 	if (!entry) {
1181 | 		return;
1182 | 	}
1183 | 	if (entry.expiresAt <= Date.now()) {
1184 | 		roleCache.delete(userId);
1185 | 		return;
1186 | 	}
1187 | 	return {
1188 | 		banExpires: entry.banExpires,
1189 | 		banReason: entry.banReason,
1190 | 		banned: entry.banned,
1191 | 		clinicId: entry.clinicId,
1192 | 		role: entry.role
1193 | 	};
1194 | }
1195 | 
1196 | export function setCachedRole(
1197 | 	userId: string,
1198 | 	role: Role,
1199 | 	clinicId: string | null, // ← was `string`; preserves null
1200 | 	banned = false,
1201 | 	banReason: string | null = null,
1202 | 	banExpires: Date | null = null
1203 | ): void {
1204 | 	if (!userId) {
1205 | 		return;
1206 | 	}
1207 | 	if (!role) {
1208 | 		roleCache.delete(userId);
1209 | 		return;
1210 | 	}
1211 | 	roleCache.set(userId, {
1212 | 		banExpires,
1213 | 		banReason,
1214 | 		banned,
1215 | 		clinicId, // ← store as-is; don't coerce "" ← null
1216 | 		expiresAt: Date.now() + ROLE_CACHE_TTL_MS,
1217 | 		role
1218 | 	});
1219 | }
1220 | 
1221 | /** Evict expired entries. Safe to call from a timer or manually. */
1222 | export function sweepRoleCache(): void {
1223 | 	const now = Date.now();
1224 | 	for (const [userId, entry] of roleCache) {
1225 | 		if (entry.expiresAt <= now) {
1226 | 			roleCache.delete(userId);
1227 | 		}
1228 | 	}
1229 | }
1230 | 
1231 | /** Invalidate one user (used by role updates, bans, deletes). */
1232 | export function invalidateCachedRole(userId: string): void {
1233 | 	roleCache.delete(userId);
1234 | }

1790 |  * are structurally identical but nominally distinct under TypeScript, and

1794 | 
1795 | export const userRoleSchema = z.enum(USER_ROLES);
1796 | export type Role = z.infer<typeof userRoleSchema>;
1797 | 
1798 | export const rolesMapSchema = z.record(z.string(), userRoleSchema);
1799 | export type RolesMap = z.infer<typeof rolesMapSchema>;

1835 | interface CachedRole {
1836 | 	role: Role;
1837 | 	banned: boolean;
1838 | 	banReason: string | null;
1839 | 	clinicId: string | null;
1840 | 	banExpires: Date | null;
1841 | 	expiresAt: number;
1842 | }
1843 | 
1844 | const ROLE_CACHE_TTL_MS = 60_000;
1845 | const roleCache = new Map<string, CachedRole>();
1846 | 
1847 | export function getCachedRole(userId: string) {
1848 | 	const entry = roleCache.get(userId);
1849 | 	if (!entry) {
1850 | 		return;
1851 | 	}
1852 | 	if (entry.expiresAt <= Date.now()) {
1853 | 		roleCache.delete(userId);
1854 | 		return;
1855 | 	}
1856 | 	return {
1857 | 		banExpires: entry.banExpires,
1858 | 		banReason: entry.banReason,
1859 | 		banned: entry.banned,
1860 | 		clinicId: entry.clinicId,
1861 | 		role: entry.role
1862 | 	};
1863 | }
1864 | 
1865 | export function setCachedRole(
1866 | 	userId: string,
1867 | 	role: Role,
1868 | 	clinicId: string | null, // ← was `string`; preserves null
1869 | 	banned = false,
1870 | 	banReason: string | null = null,
1871 | 	banExpires: Date | null = null
1872 | ): void {
1873 | 	if (!userId) {
1874 | 		return;
1875 | 	}
1876 | 	if (!role) {
1877 | 		roleCache.delete(userId);
1878 | 		return;
1879 | 	}
1880 | 	roleCache.set(userId, {
1881 | 		banExpires,
1882 | 		banReason,
1883 | 		banned,
1884 | 		clinicId, // ← store as-is; don't coerce "" ← null
1885 | 		expiresAt: Date.now() + ROLE_CACHE_TTL_MS,
1886 | 		role
1887 | 	});
1888 | }
1889 | 
1890 | /** Evict expired entries. Safe to call from a timer or manually. */
1891 | export function sweepRoleCache(): void {
1892 | 	const now = Date.now();
1893 | 	for (const [userId, entry] of roleCache) {
1894 | 		if (entry.expiresAt <= now) {
1895 | 			roleCache.delete(userId);
1896 | 		}
1897 | 	}
1898 | }
1899 | 
1900 | /** Invalidate one user (used by role updates, bans, deletes). */
1901 | export function invalidateCachedRole(userId: string): void {
1902 | 	roleCache.delete(userId);
1903 | }

```ts
   1 | import { z } from "zod";
   2 | 
   3 | /**
   4 |  * Canonical role vocabulary.
   5 |  *
   6 |  * ⚠️ This is the single source of truth for user roles. `schemas/enums.ts`
   7 |  * re-exports `USER_ROLES` and `userRoleSchema` from here — do NOT define a
   8 |  * second list there. Two enums with the same members but different order
   9 |  * are structurally identical but nominally distinct under TypeScript, and
  10 |  * `UserRole`/`Role` would stop being assignable to each other.
  11 |  */
  12 | export const USER_ROLES = ["admin", "doctor", "staff", "guardian", "patient"] as const;
  13 | 
  14 | export const userRoleSchema = z.enum(USER_ROLES);
  15 | export type Role = z.infer<typeof userRoleSchema>;
  16 | 
  17 | export const rolesMapSchema = z.record(z.string(), userRoleSchema);
  18 | export type RolesMap = z.infer<typeof rolesMapSchema>;
  19 | 
  20 | export const ROLES_MAP = {
  21 |   ADMIN: "admin",
  22 |   DOCTOR: "doctor",
  23 |   STAFF: "staff",
  24 |   GUARDIAN: "guardian",
  25 |   PATIENT: "patient",
  26 | } as const satisfies RolesMap;
```

```ts
  21 | interface CachedRole {
  22 |   role: Role;
  23 |   banned: boolean;
  24 |   banReason: string | null;
  25 |   clinicId: string | null;
  26 |   banExpires: Date | null;
  27 |   expiresAt: number;
  28 | }
  29 | 
  30 | const ROLE_CACHE_TTL_MS = 60_000;
  31 | const roleCache = new Map<string, CachedRole>();
  32 | 
  33 | export function getCachedRole(userId: string) {
  34 |   const entry = roleCache.get(userId);
  35 |   if (!entry) {
  36 |     return;
  37 |   }
  38 |   if (entry.expiresAt <= Date.now()) {
  39 |     roleCache.delete(userId);
  40 |     return;
  41 |   }
  42 |   return {
  43 |     banExpires: entry.banExpires,
  44 |     banReason: entry.banReason,
  45 |     banned: entry.banned,
  46 |     clinicId: entry.clinicId,
  47 |     role: entry.role,
  48 |   };
  49 | }
  50 | 
  51 | export function setCachedRole(
  52 |   userId: string,
  53 |   role: Role,
  54 |   clinicId: string | null, // ← was `string`; preserves null
  55 |   banned = false,
  56 |   banReason: string | null = null,
  57 |   banExpires: Date | null = null,
  58 | ): void {
  59 |   if (!userId) {
  60 |     return;
  61 |   }
  62 |   if (!role) {
  63 |     roleCache.delete(userId);
  64 |     return;
  65 |   }
  66 |   roleCache.set(userId, {
  67 |     banExpires,
  68 |     banReason,
  69 |     banned,
  70 |     clinicId, // ← store as-is; don't coerce "" ← null
  71 |     expiresAt: Date.now() + ROLE_CACHE_TTL_MS,
  72 |     role,
  73 |   });
  74 | }
  75 | 
  76 | /** Evict expired entries. Safe to call from a timer or manually. */
  77 | export function sweepRoleCache(): void {
  78 |   const now = Date.now();
  79 |   for (const [userId, entry] of roleCache) {
  80 |     if (entry.expiresAt <= now) {
  81 |       roleCache.delete(userId);
  82 |     }
  83 |   }
  84 | }
  85 | 
  86 | /** Invalidate one user (used by role updates, bans, deletes). */
  87 | export function invalidateCachedRole(userId: string): void {
  88 |   roleCache.delete(userId);
  89 | }
  90 | 
  91 | export const EMAIL_REGEX = /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/;
```

```ts
   1 | export type ErrorKind = "not-found" | "permission" | "network" | "unknown";
   2 | 
   3 | export function classifyError(err: unknown): ErrorKind {
   4 |   if (err && typeof err === "object") {
   5 |     const status = (err as { status?: number }).status;
   6 |     const code = (err as { code?: string }).code;
   7 |     if (status === 404 || code === "NOT_FOUND") return "not-found";
   8 |     if (status === 401 || status === 403 || code === "FORBIDDEN") return "permission";
   9 |     if (
  10 |       (typeof navigator !== "undefined" && !navigator.onLine) ||
  11 |       (err instanceof TypeError && /fetch|network/i.test(err.message))
  12 |     )
  13 |       return "network";
  14 |   }
  15 |   return "unknown";
  16 | }
```

```ts
   1 | import * as React from "react";
   2 | 
   3 | export function composeRefs<T>(...refs: Array<React.Ref<T> | undefined>): React.RefCallback<T> {
   4 |   return (node: T) => {
   5 |     refs.forEach((ref) => {
   6 |       if (typeof ref === "function") {
   7 |         ref(node);
   8 |       } else if (ref != null) {
   9 |         (ref as React.RefObject<T>).current = node;
  10 |       }
  11 |     });
  12 |   };
  13 | }
  14 | 
  15 | export function useComposedRefs<T>(...refs: Array<React.Ref<T> | undefined>): React.RefCallback<T> {
  16 |   // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps -- refs is a rest param, memoized per call site
  17 |   return React.useCallback(composeRefs(...refs), [...refs]);
  18 | }
  19 | 
  20 | export function composeEventHandlers<E>(
  21 |   originalEventHandler?: (event: E) => void,
  22 |   ourEventHandler?: (event: E) => void,
  23 |   { checkForDefaultPrevented = true } = {},
  24 | ) {
  25 |   return function handleEvent(event: E) {
  26 |     originalEventHandler?.(event);
  27 | 
  28 |     if (
  29 |       checkForDefaultPrevented === false ||
  30 |       !(event as unknown as { defaultPrevented: boolean })?.defaultPrevented
  31 |     ) {
  32 |       return ourEventHandler?.(event);
  33 |     }
  34 |   };
  35 | }
```

```ts
   1 | /**
   2 |  * src/lib/dates.ts
   3 |  *
   4 |  * Canonical date/time formatting utilities. Every screen that shows a date or
   5 |  * time to a user should use one of these functions so the output is consistent
   6 |  * across the application and respects the zone passed in.
   7 |  *
   8 |  * Rules:
   9 |  *  - Never call `toLocaleDateString`, `toLocaleString`, or construct a raw
  10 |  *    `Intl.DateTimeFormat` in component code. Use these helpers instead.
  11 |  *  - For stored patterns such as `yyyy-MM-dd`, using them directly in code is
  12 |  *    fine — the rule only applies to human-readable output.
  13 |  */
  14 | 
  15 | // ─── Short-date: "Jan 5, 2024" ────────────────────────────────────────────
  16 | const SHORT_DATE_FMT = new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", {
  17 |   year: "numeric",
  18 |   month: "short",
  19 |   day: "numeric",
  20 | });
  21 | 
  22 | /** "Jan 5, 2024" */
  23 | export function formatDate(date: Date): string {
  24 |   return SHORT_DATE_FMT.format(date);
  25 | }
  26 | 
  27 | export function formatWeekRange(start: Date, end: Date): string {
  28 |   const startFmt = new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", {
  29 |     month: "short",
  30 |     day: "numeric",
  31 |   });
  32 |   const endFmt = new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", {
  33 |     month: "short",
  34 |     day: "numeric",
  35 |     year: "numeric",
  36 |   });
  37 |   return `${startFmt.format(start)} – ${endFmt.format(end)}`;
  38 | }
  39 | // ─── Short-time: "14:35" ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
  40 | const SHORT_TIME_FMT = new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-GB", {
  41 |   hour: "2-digit",
  42 |   minute: "2-digit",
  43 |   hour12: false,
  44 | });
  45 |

  47 | export function formatTime(date: Date): string {
  48 |   return SHORT_TIME_FMT.format(date);
  49 | }

  53 |   year: "numeric",
  54 |   month: "short",
  55 |   day: "numeric",
  56 |   hour: "2-digit",
  57 |   minute: "2-digit",
  58 | });
  59 |

 101 | /** "Monday, 5 January 2024" */
 102 | export function formatDayHeadingWithYear(date: Date): string {
 103 |   return DAY_HEADING_YEAR_FMT.format(date);
 104 | }
 105 | 
 106 | // ─── Local date: "2024-01-05" ─────────────────────────────────────────────
 107 | /**
 108 |  * "2024-01-05" — a local-time yyyy-MM-dd string, suitable for `<input type="date">`.
 109 |  * Not the same as `.toISOString().slice(0,10)` which is always UTC.
 110 |  */
 111 | export function formatLocalDate(date: Date): string {
 112 |   const y = date.getFullYear();
 113 |   const m = String(date.getMonth() + 1).padStart(2, "0");
 114 |   const d = String(date.getDate()).padStart(2, "0");
 115 |   return `${y}-${m}-${d}`;
 116 | }
 117 | 
 118 | // ─── Month heading: "January 2024" ────────────────────────────────────────
 119 | const MONTH_FMT = new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-GB", {
 120 |   month: "long",
 121 |   year: "numeric",
 122 | });
 123 | 
 124 | /** "January 2024" */
 125 | export function formatMonth(date: Date): string {
 126 |   return MONTH_FMT.format(date);
 127 | }
 128 | 
 129 | // ─── Prompt-style "now": "Monday, 5 Jan 2024 at 14:35" ────────────────────
 130 | /**
 131 |  * A verbose, unambiguous representation for use in AI prompts or audit logs.
 132 |  * Includes weekday, date, and time.
 133 |  */
 134 | export function formatPromptNow(date: Date = new Date()): string {
 135 |   return new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-GB", {
 136 |     weekday: "long",
 137 |     day: "numeric",
 138 |     month: "short",
 139 |     year: "numeric",
 140 |     hour: "2-digit",
 141 |     minute: "2-digit",
 142 |     hour12: false,
 143 |   }).format(date);
 144 | }
 145 | export function formatStatusLabel(status: string): string {
 146 |   return status.replace(/_/g, " ").replace(/\b\w/g, (c) => c.toUpperCase());
 147 | }
 148 | // Date helpers shared by the calendar, the week strip, and the queue.
 149 | 
 150 | export function startOfDay(d: Date): Date {
 151 |   const r = new Date(d);
 152 |   r.setHours(0, 0, 0, 0);
 153 |   return r;
 154 | }
 155 | 
 156 | export function addDays(d: Date, n: number): Date {
 157 |   const r = new Date(d);
 158 |   r.setDate(r.getDate() + n);
 159 |   return r;
 160 | }
 161 | 
 162 | export function startOfWeek(d: Date): Date {
 163 |   const r = startOfDay(d);
 164 |   const day = r.getDay();
 165 |   r.setDate(r.getDate() - (day === 0 ? 6 : day - 1));
 166 |   return r;
 167 | }
 168 | 
 169 | export function startOfMonth(d: Date): Date {
 170 |   return new Date(d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth(), 1);
 171 | }
 172 | 
 173 | export function isSameDay(a: Date, b: Date): boolean {
 174 |   return (
 175 |     a.getDate() === b.getDate() &&
 176 |     a.getMonth() === b.getMonth() &&
 177 |     a.getFullYear() === b.getFullYear()
 178 |   );
 179 | }
 180 | 
 181 | export function toDateKey(d: Date | string): string {
 182 |   const date = startOfDay(new Date(d));
 183 |   return `${date.getFullYear()}-${String(date.getMonth() + 1).padStart(2, "0")}-${String(date.getDate()).padStart(2, "0")}`;
 184 | }
 185 | 
 186 | export function toLocalDateTimeString(date: Date): string {
 187 |   const pad = (n: number) => String(n).padStart(2, "0");
 188 |   return `${date.getFullYear()}-${pad(date.getMonth() + 1)}-${pad(date.getDate())}T${pad(date.getHours())}:${pad(date.getMinutes())}`;
 189 | }
 190 | 
 191 | export function nowLocalInput(offsetMinutes = 0): string {
 192 |   return new Date(Date.now() + offsetMinutes * 60_000 - new Date().getTimezoneOffset() * 60_000)
 193 |     .toISOString()
 194 |     .slice(0, 16);
 195 | }
 196 | 
 197 | export function roundToNextSlot(offsetMin = 30): string {
 198 |   const d = new Date(Date.now() + offsetMin * 60_000);
 199 |   d.setMinutes(Math.ceil(d.getMinutes() / 15) * 15, 0, 0);
 200 |   return toLocalDateTimeString(d);
 201 | }
 202 | 
 203 | /** True for any of the "the appointment no longer needs action" states. */
 204 | export function isFinishedStatus(status: string): boolean {
 205 |   return status === "completed" || status === "cancelled" || status === "no-show";
 206 | }
 207 | 
 208 | /** True when a key event landed on a form field. */
 209 | export function isEditableTarget(el: Element | null): boolean {
 210 |   if (!(el instanceof HTMLElement)) return false;
 211 |   if (el instanceof HTMLInputElement) return true;
 212 |   if (el instanceof HTMLTextAreaElement) return true;
 213 |   if (el instanceof HTMLSelectElement) return true;
 214 |   if (el.isContentEditable) return true;
 215 |   return false;
 216 | }
 217 | export function groupByDay<T extends { scheduledAt: Date | string }>(
 218 |   appointments: T[],
 219 | ): Record<string, T[]> {
 220 |   const groups: Record<string, T[]> = {};
 221 |   for (const appt of appointments) {
 222 |     const key = toDateKey(appt.scheduledAt);
 223 |     if (!groups[key]) {
 224 |       groups[key] = [];
 225 |     }
 226 |     groups[key].push(appt);
 227 |   }
 228 |   return groups;
 229 | }
```

```tsx
  47 | function getLanguage(language: string) {
  48 |   const name = language.toLowerCase();
  49 | 
  50 |   if (name === "ansi") {
  51 |     return name;
  52 |   }
  53 | 
  54 |   if (name in languages) {
  55 |     return name as keyof typeof languages;
  56 |   }
  57 | 
  58 |   return aliases[name] ?? null;
  59 | }
  60 | 
  61 | // Loads a language and returns a highlighter for it, or null for a language
  62 | // that is not listed.
  63 | export async function loadHighlighter(language: string) {
  64 |   const lang = getLanguage(language);
  65 | 
  66 |   if (!lang) {
  67 |     return null;
  68 |   }
  69 | 
  70 |   const shiki = await getHighlighter();
  71 | 
  72 |   if (lang !== "ansi" && !shiki.getLoadedLanguages().includes(lang)) {
  73 |     await shiki.loadLanguage(languages[lang]);
  74 |   }
  75 | 
  76 |   return {
  77 |     // Returns one React node per line, and the grammar state after the last
  78 |     // line. Pass that state back to continue where the code left off.
  79 |     highlight(code: string, state?: GrammarState) {
  80 |       const tokenize = (text: string) =>
  81 |         shiki.codeToTokens(text, {
  82 |           lang,
  83 |           themes: { light: "github-light", dark: "github-dark" },
  84 |           defaultColor: false,
  85 |           grammarState: state,
  86 |         }).tokens;
  87 | 
  88 |       // ANSI has no grammar state, so each line is tokenized on its own and
  89 |       // gets the same colors whether it arrives in one piece or streams.
  90 |       const tokens =
  91 |         lang === "ansi" ? code.split("\n").flatMap((line) => tokenize(line)) : tokenize(code);
  92 | 
  93 |       return {
  94 |         lines: tokens.map((line) =>
  95 |           line.map((token, index) => (
  96 |             <span
  97 |               className="text-(--shiki-light) dark:text-(--shiki-dark)"
  98 |               key={index}
  99 |               style={token.htmlStyle as React.CSSProperties}
 100 |             >
 101 |               {token.content}
 102 |             </span>
 103 |           )),
 104 |         ),
 105 |         state: shiki.getLastGrammarState(tokens),
 106 |       };
 107 |     },
 108 |   };
 109 | }
 110 | 
 111 | // Returns one React node per line, or null for a language that is not listed.
 112 | export async function highlightCode(code: string, language: string) {
 113 |   const highlighter = await loadHighlighter(language);
 114 | 
 115 |   return highlighter ? highlighter.highlight(code).lines : null;
 116 | }
```

`lib/server/idempotency.ts`:

```ts
   1 | // src/lib/server/idempotency.ts
   2 | import { db } from "@/db";
   3 | import { idempotency } from "@/db/schema";
   4 | 
   5 | /**
   6 |  * Wraps a server function so a repeated call with the same
   7 |  * Idempotency-Key returns the cached response instead of re-executing.
   8 |  *
   9 |  * - Cache TTL is 24h. Long enough to cover a full offline session.
  10 |  * - Cache is keyed by (idempotencyKey) globally. Add a `userId` or
  11 |  *   `clinicId` to the key if you want per-tenant isolation.
  12 |  * - Stores the *result* of a successful call AND the shape of a 409
  13 |  *   conflict, so retries of a conflict don't re-hit the DB.
  14 |  */
  15 | export type IdempotentResult<T> =
  16 |   | { kind: "ok"; data: T }
  17 |   | { kind: "conflict"; serverSnapshot: unknown };
  18 | 
  19 | export async function withIdempotency<T>(
  20 |   idempotencyKey: string | null,
  21 |   handler: () => Promise<IdempotentResult<T>>,
  22 | ): Promise<IdempotentResult<T>> {
  23 |   if (!idempotencyKey) {
  24 |     // No key → cannot dedupe. We still run, but warn so you notice
  25 |     // a caller that forgot to pass the header.
  26 |     console.warn("[idempotency] missing Idempotency-Key — retries will duplicate");
  27 |     return handler();
  28 |   }
  29 | 
  30 |   const existing = await db.query.idempotency.findFirst({
  31 |     where: { key: idempotencyKey },
  32 |   });
  33 |   if (existing) {
  34 |     return existing.result as IdempotentResult<T>;
  35 |   }
  36 | 
  37 |   const result = await handler();
  38 | 
  39 |   // Only cache successful writes AND 409s. A retryable network error
  40 |   // must NOT be cached — the next attempt should re-run.
  41 |   if (result.kind === "ok" || result.kind === "conflict") {
  42 |     await db.insert(idempotency).values({
  43 |       id: crypto.randomUUID(),
  44 |       key: idempotencyKey,
  45 |       requestHash: idempotencyKey,
  46 |       result: result as object,
  47 |       createdAt: new Date(),
  48 |     });
  49 |   }
  50 | 
  51 |   return result;
  52 | }
```

```ts
   1 | // The page numbers to show around the current one, with gaps where pages are skipped.
   2 | export function pageRange(current: number, total: number, siblings = 1): (number | "gap")[] {
   3 |   if (total <= 3 + siblings * 2) return Array.from({ length: total }, (_, index) => index + 1);
   4 | 
   5 |   const around = Array.from({ length: siblings * 2 + 1 }, (_, index) => current - siblings + index);
   6 |   const pages = new Set([1, ...around, total]);
   7 |   const sorted = [...pages].filter((page) => page >= 1 && page <= total).toSorted((a, b) => a - b);
   8 | 
   9 |   return sorted.flatMap((page, index) => {
  10 |     const previous = sorted[index - 1];
  11 |     return previous !== undefined && page - previous > 1 ? ["gap" as const, page] : [page];
  12 |   });
  13 | }
```

```ts
   1 | // src/lib/shadcn/theme-init.ts
   2 | //
   3 | // The pre-paint theme initializer. Kept out of `__root.tsx` so that
   4 | // file reads as routing + shell only, and so the string can be unit-
   5 | // tested in isolation (or linted for banned constructs like
   6 | // `eval` / `document.write`).
   7 | //
   8 | // Contract with `lib/shadcn/theme-utils.ts`:
   9 | //   - storage key:   "theme"  (THEME_STORAGE_KEY)
  10 | //   - valid values:  "light" | "dark" | "system"  (Theme)
  11 | //   - fallback:      "system"
  12 | //   - applies:       <html class="light|dark"> + <html style="color-scheme">
  13 | //   - does NOT touch: data-theme, meta[theme-color]  (both handled
  14 | //     declaratively in `head()` on the root route)
  15 | //
  16 | // If you change any of the above, change it here AND in theme-utils.ts.
  17 | // The two cannot share code (this runs before any module loads), so the
  18 | // invariant is documented, not enforced. Add a unit test that asserts
  19 | // both files agree — that's the only real guard.
  20 | 
  21 | export const THEME_INIT_SCRIPT = `
  22 | (function(){
  23 | 	try{
  24 | 		var s = localStorage.getItem('theme');
  25 | 		var m = (s === 'light' || s === 'dark' || s === 'system') ? s : 'system';
  26 | 		var prefersDark = matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches;
  27 | 		var resolved = m === 'system' ? (prefersDark ? 'dark' : 'light') : m;
  28 | 		var e = document.documentElement;
  29 | 		e.classList.remove('light', 'dark');
  30 | 		e.classList.add(resolved);
  31 | 		e.style.colorScheme = resolved;
  32 | 	} catch (err) {}
  33 | })();
  34 | `.replace(/\n\s*/g, "");
```

```ts
   1 | // src/lib/shadcn/theme-utils.ts
   2 | //
   3 | // Non-component theme logic. Split from `theme.tsx` so that file can
   4 | // export only `<ThemeProvider />` and stay fast-refresh friendly.
   5 | //
   6 | // Two invariants this file maintains:
   7 | //
   8 | //   1. `resolveTheme` is the *single* place that turns a `Theme` into a
   9 | //      `ResolvedTheme`. `applyTheme` (client, post-hydration) and
  10 | //      `getThemeScript` (inline SSR script, pre-hydration) both encode the
  11 | //      same rule. Centralising it means a default flip can't desync them.
  12 | //
  13 | //   2. Every browser API is guarded. `localStorage`, `matchMedia`, and
  14 | //      `document.documentElement` are undefined during SSR, absent in
  15 | //      some privacy modes, and throw in jsdom unless polyfilled. A
  16 | //      utility that crashes the whole page because the user has
  17 | //      "block all cookies" enabled is not production-ready.
  18 | 
  19 | import type { ResolvedTheme, Theme } from "./theme-context";
  20 | 
  21 | // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  22 | // Constants
  23 | // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  24 | 
  25 | /** Key shared by the inline SSR script and React's `useEffect` hooks. */
  26 | export const THEME_STORAGE_KEY = "theme";
  27 | 
  28 | /** The canonical set of valid `Theme` values. */
  29 | const THEME_VALUES: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set<Theme>(["dark", "light", "system"]);
  30 | 
  31 | /** Fallback used when storage is empty, unreadable, or holds garbage. */
  32 | const FALLBACK_THEME: Theme = "system";
  33 | 
  34 | /**
  35 |  * The two class names applied to `<html>`. Kept as constants so
  36 |  * `applyTheme` and the DOM cleanup path can't drift.
  37 |  */
  38 | const LIGHT_CLASS = "light";
  39 | const DARK_CLASS = "dark";
  40 | const ALL_THEME_CLASSES = [LIGHT_CLASS, DARK_CLASS] as const;
  41 | 
  42 | // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  43 | // Validation
  44 | // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  45 | 
  46 | /**
  47 |  * True iff `value` is a string that names a valid `Theme`.
  48 |  *
  49 |  * Narrows `string | null` to `Theme`, so callers get exhaustiveness for
  50 |  * free. The `null` check is inside the guard because `THEME_VALUES.has`
  51 |  * would accept `null` at runtime, and `null` is not a `Theme`.
  52 |  */
  53 | export function isTheme(value: unknown): value is Theme {
  54 |   return typeof value === "string" && THEME_VALUES.has(value);
  55 | }
  56 | 
  57 | // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  58 | // Storage
  59 | // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  60 | 
  61 | /**
  62 |  * Read the persisted theme. Returns the fallback if:
  63 |  *   - there is no storage (`localStorage` undefined — SSR, sandbox),
  64 |  *   - reading throws (Safari private mode, blocked cookies, quota),
  65 |  *   - the stored value is missing or not a valid `Theme`.
  66 |  *
  67 |  * Never throws. Callers don't need try/catch around it.
  68 |  */
  69 | export function readStoredTheme(storageKey: string = THEME_STORAGE_KEY): Theme {
  70 |   try {
  71 |     if (typeof window === "undefined") return FALLBACK_THEME;
  72 |     const raw = window.localStorage.getItem(storageKey);
  73 |     return isTheme(raw) ? raw : FALLBACK_THEME;
  74 |   } catch {
  75 |     return FALLBACK_THEME;
  76 |   }
  77 | }
  78 | 
  79 | /**
  80 |  * Persist the theme. Silent on failure — the in-memory `useState` in the
  81 |  * provider keeps the choice for this session; storage is a durability
  82 |  * optimisation, not the source of truth.
  83 |  *
  84 |  * Returns `true` on success so callers that care (e.g. the cross-tab
  85 |  * `StorageEvent` listener) can skip a redundant state update if the
  86 |  * write was rejected and the value didn't change.
  87 |  */
  88 | export function writeStoredTheme(theme: Theme, storageKey: string = THEME_STORAGE_KEY): boolean {
  89 |   try {
  90 |     if (typeof window === "undefined") return false;
  91 |     window.localStorage.setItem(storageKey, theme);
  92 |     return true;
  93 |   } catch {
  94 |     return false;
  95 |   }
  96 | }
  97 | 
  98 | // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  99 | // Resolution — the single source of truth for `theme → resolved`
 100 | // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 101 | 
 102 | /**
 103 |  * Resolve a `Theme` to the concrete `ResolvedTheme` ("light" | "dark").
 104 |  *
 105 |  * - `"light"` / `"dark"` pass through unchanged.
 106 |  * - `"system"` reads `prefers-color-scheme` *once*. If `matchMedia` is
 107 |  *   unavailable (SSR, jsdom without a mock), returns `"light"` — a
 108 |  *   deliberate, documented default. Dark-by-default would cause a
 109 |  *   visible flash for the vast majority of users (light-mode is still
 110 |  *   the OS default), so light-as-fallback is the safer choice.
 111 |  */
 112 | export function resolveTheme(theme: Theme): ResolvedTheme {
 113 |   if (theme !== "system") return theme;
 114 | 
 115 |   if (typeof window === "undefined" || typeof window.matchMedia !== "function") {
 116 |     return "light";
 117 |   }
 118 | 
 119 |   try {
 120 |     return window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches ? "dark" : "light";
 121 |   } catch {
 122 |     // Older or embedded browsers can throw on the media query itself.
 123 |     return "light";
 124 |   }
 125 | }
 126 | 
 127 | // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 128 | // DOM application
 129 | // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 130 | 
 131 | /**
 132 |  * Apply the resolved theme to `<html>`: swap the `light`/`dark` class and
 133 |  * set `color-scheme` so native form controls (inputs, scrollbars) follow.
 134 |  *
 135 |  * Idempotent. Safe to call on every render — the cost is two
 136 |  * `classList` reads and one write. Guarded so it can be called from a
 137 |  * `useEffect` during SSR without crashing (returns `false` there).
 138 |  *
 139 |  * Returns `true` if the DOM was updated, `false` if we're on the server.
 140 |  */
 141 | export function applyTheme(theme: Theme): boolean {
 142 |   if (typeof document === "undefined") return false;
 143 | 
 144 |   const resolved = resolveTheme(theme);
 145 |   const root = document.documentElement;
 146 | 
 147 |   // Remove both, then add one. This is atomic enough for the class
 148 |   // attribute (a single mutation target) and avoids the "remove then
 149 |   // add leaves a frame with neither class" flicker that a naive
 150 |   // `remove(prev); add(next)` would produce on slower devices.
 151 |   for (const className of ALL_THEME_CLASSES) {
 152 |     root.classList.remove(className);
 153 |   }
 154 |   root.classList.add(resolved);
 155 |   root.style.colorScheme = resolved;
 156 | 
 157 |   return true;
 158 | }
 159 | 
 160 | // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 161 | // Inline SSR script
 162 | // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 163 | 
 164 | /**
 165 |  * Build the tiny inline script that runs before React hydrates, so the
 166 |  * first paint matches the persisted theme.
 167 |  *
 168 |  * The script body deliberately duplicates `readStoredTheme` +
 169 |  * `resolveTheme` + `applyTheme` because it must run before any JS module
 170 |  * is loaded — it can't import this file. The `ResolvedTheme` mapping and
 171 |  * the class names are the only things that must stay in sync, and both
 172 |  * are covered by the `resolveTheme` docstring above.
 173 |  *
 174 |  * Security: `storageKey` and `defaultTheme` are serialised with
 175 |  * `JSON.stringify`, so a caller passing a key containing `</script>`
 176 |  * cannot break out of the script tag.
 177 |  */
 178 | export function getThemeScript(
 179 |   storageKey: string = THEME_STORAGE_KEY,
 180 |   defaultTheme: Theme = FALLBACK_THEME,
 181 | ): string {
 182 |   const key = JSON.stringify(storageKey);
 183 |   const fallback = JSON.stringify(defaultTheme);
 184 |   const light = JSON.stringify(LIGHT_CLASS);
 185 |   const dark = JSON.stringify(DARK_CLASS);
 186 | 
 187 |   // One line per logical step so errors in a browser console point at
 188 |   // the exact failure. Wrapped in try/catch so a blocked storage or a
 189 |   // missing `matchMedia` silently falls back to light, matching
 190 |   // `resolveTheme`'s behaviour.
 191 |   return `(function(){try{
 192 | 		var s=window.localStorage.getItem(${key});
 193 | 		var valid=s==="light"||s==="dark"||s==="system";
 194 | 		var t=valid?s:${fallback};
 195 | 		var r=t;
 196 | 		if(t==="system"){
 197 | 			r=window.matchMedia&&window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches?${dark}:${light};
 198 | 		}
 199 | 		var e=document.documentElement;
 200 | 		e.classList.remove(${light},${dark});
 201 | 		e.classList.add(r);
 202 | 		e.style.colorScheme=r;
 203 | 	}catch(_e){}})();`;
 204 | }
```

```tsx
   1 | // src/lib/shadcn/theme.tsx
   2 | 
   3 | import { ScriptOnce } from "@tanstack/react-router";
   4 | import { useCallback, useEffect, useState, useSyncExternalStore } from "react";
   5 | 
   6 | import { type ResolvedTheme, type Theme, ThemeContext } from "./theme-context";
   7 | import {
   8 |   applyTheme,
   9 |   getThemeScript,
  10 |   isTheme,
  11 |   readStoredTheme,
  12 |   resolveTheme,
  13 |   THEME_STORAGE_KEY,
  14 |   writeStoredTheme,
  15 | } from "./theme-utils";
  16 | 
  17 | export type ThemeProviderProps = {
  18 |   children: React.ReactNode;
  19 |   defaultTheme?: Theme;
  20 |   storageKey?: string;
  21 | };
  22 | 
  23 | // `useSyncExternalStore` is the SSR-safe way to read "am I on the
  24 | // server?". `getServerSnapshot` returns `true` during SSR and
  25 | // `false` on the client. Unlike `typeof window !== "undefined"`,
  26 | // this is stable across the hydration boundary and won't trigger a
  27 | // hydration mismatch warning.
  28 | const emptySubscribe = () => () => {};
  29 | const getServerSnapshot = () => true;
  30 | const getClientSnapshot = () => false;
  31 | 
  32 | /**
  33 |  * The single `<ThemeProvider />` in the app.
  34 |  *
  35 |  * Provides the **same** `ThemeContext` that `hooks/use-theme.ts` reads.
  36 |  * Injects the SSR script so the first paint matches the resolved
  37 |  * theme, and keeps `<html class>` in sync with the persisted choice.
  38 |  *
  39 |  * `ScriptOnce` is only meaningful during SSR — it emits a `<script>`
  40 |  * tag into the server-rendered `<head>`. On the client, and in any
  41 |  * non-router tree (tests, isolated stories), it calls `useRouter()`
  42 |  * and crashes because there's no router above it. We gate it on the
  43 |  * environment so the SSR injection still happens and the client path
  44 |  * stays router-free.
  45 |  */
  46 | export function ThemeProvider({
  47 |   children,
  48 |   defaultTheme = "system",
  49 |   storageKey = THEME_STORAGE_KEY,
  50 | }: ThemeProviderProps) {
  51 |   const isServer = useSyncExternalStore(emptySubscribe, getClientSnapshot, getServerSnapshot);
  52 | 
  53 |   const [theme, setThemeState] = useState<Theme>(defaultTheme);
  54 |   const [mounted, setMounted] = useState(false);
  55 | 
  56 |   // Hydrate the persisted theme on mount. Reading storage during
  57 |   // render would be a hydration mismatch — this effect runs after
  58 |   // SSR markup is committed.
  59 |   useEffect(() => {
  60 |     // Read the persisted choice after mount so the first client render stays
  61 |     // consistent with the SSR output and avoids a hydration mismatch.
  62 |     // eslint-disable-next-line react/set-state-in-effect -- this sync is intentionally tied to client mount and storage hydration.
  63 |     setThemeState(readStoredTheme(storageKey));
  64 |     setMounted(true);
  65 |   }, [storageKey]);
  66 | 
  67 |   // Apply the theme to <html> once mounted, and on every change.
  68 |   useEffect(() => {
  69 |     if (!mounted) return;
  70 |     applyTheme(theme);
  71 |   }, [theme, mounted]);
  72 | 
  73 |   // When the user follows the system, listen for OS-level changes
  74 |   // and re-apply. `resolveTheme` centralises the mapping so this
  75 |   // file can't disagree with the inline init script (theme-init.ts).
  76 |   useEffect(() => {
  77 |     if (!mounted || theme !== "system") return;
  78 | 
  79 |     if (typeof window.matchMedia !== "function") return;
  80 |     const media = window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)");
  81 |     const onChange = () => applyTheme(resolveTheme("system"));
  82 |     media.addEventListener("change", onChange);
  83 |     return () => media.removeEventListener("change", onChange);
  84 |   }, [theme, mounted]);
  85 | 
  86 |   // Cross-tab sync — the test file exercises this via `StorageEvent`.
  87 |   useEffect(() => {
  88 |     const onStorage = (event: StorageEvent) => {
  89 |       if (event.key !== storageKey) return;
  90 |       const nextTheme = isTheme(event.newValue) ? event.newValue : readStoredTheme(storageKey);
  91 |       setThemeState(nextTheme);
  92 |       applyTheme(nextTheme);
  93 |     };
  94 |     window.addEventListener("storage", onStorage);
  95 |     return () => window.removeEventListener("storage", onStorage);
  96 |   }, [storageKey]);
  97 | 
  98 |   const setTheme = useCallback(
  99 |     (next: Theme) => {
 100 |       writeStoredTheme(next, storageKey);
 101 |       setThemeState(next);
 102 |     },
 103 |     [storageKey],
 104 |   );
 105 | 
 106 |   // `mounted` gating: the very first client render must agree with
 107 |   // SSR to avoid a hydration warning on any `useTheme()` consumer
 108 |   // that isn't inside `<html suppressHydrationWarning>`. Until
 109 |   // `mounted` flips, report the SSR value ("light") regardless of
 110 |   // the live matchMedia state. Once mounted, resolve for real.
 111 |   const resolvedTheme: ResolvedTheme = !mounted ? "light" : resolveTheme(theme);
 112 | 
 113 |   const toggleTheme = useCallback(() => {
 114 |     setTheme(resolvedTheme === "dark" ? "light" : "dark");
 115 |   }, [resolvedTheme, setTheme]);
 116 | 
 117 |   // Keyboard shortcut: toggle theme with "d", but not while typing or with a modifier
 118 |   useEffect(() => {
 119 |     const handleKeyDown = (event: KeyboardEvent) => {
 120 |       if (event.key !== "d") return;
 121 |       if (event.shiftKey || event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey || event.altKey) return;
 122 |       const target = event.target as HTMLElement | null;
 123 |       if (
 124 |         target &&
 125 |         (target.tagName === "INPUT" ||
 126 |           target.tagName === "TEXTAREA" ||
 127 |           target.tagName === "SELECT" ||
 128 |           target.isContentEditable)
 129 |       ) {
 130 |         return;
 131 |       }
 132 |       toggleTheme();
 133 |     };
 134 |     window.addEventListener("keydown", handleKeyDown);
 135 |     return () => window.removeEventListener("keydown", handleKeyDown);
 136 |   }, [toggleTheme]);
 137 | 
 138 |   return (
 139 |     <ThemeContext value={{ theme, resolvedTheme, setTheme, toggleTheme }}>
 140 |       {isServer && <ScriptOnce>{getThemeScript(storageKey, defaultTheme)}</ScriptOnce>}
 141 |       {children}
 142 |     </ThemeContext>
 143 |   );
 144 | }
```

```tsx
  10 | export function createTestQueryClient() {
  11 |   const client = new QueryClient({
  12 |     defaultOptions: { queries: { retry: false }, mutations: { retry: false } },
  13 |   });
  14 |   const testUser = {
  15 |     id: "u_test",
  16 |     name: "Dr. Hazem Ali",
  17 |     email: "drhazem@example.com",
  18 |     role: "admin" as const,
  19 |     clinicId: "c_test",
  20 |   };
  21 |   client.setQueryData(["auth"], testUser);
  22 |   client.setQueryData(["auth", "user"], {
  23 |     user: testUser,
  24 |     session: { id: "s_test", userId: "u_test", clinicId: "c_test" },
  25 |   });
  26 |   return client;
  27 | }
  28 | 
  29 | // Renders the real route tree at a path, the way the app boots in index.tsx.
  30 | export async function renderRoute(initialPath = "/app") {
  31 |   const queryClient = createTestQueryClient();
  32 |   const { getRouter } = await import("@/router");
  33 |   const router = getRouter();
  34 | 
  35 |   // Point the router at the requested path before loading.
  36 |   router.history.push(initialPath);
  37 |   try {
  38 |     await router.load();
  39 |   } catch {
  40 |     // ignore redirects or offline loaders
  41 |   }
  42 | 
  43 |   const view = render(
  44 |     <ThemeProvider>
  45 |       <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
  46 |         <RouterProvider router={router} />
  47 |       </QueryClientProvider>
  48 |     </ThemeProvider>,
  49 |   );
  50 | 
  51 |   return { ...view, router, queryClient };
  52 | }
  53 |

  57 | function hasLegacyMediaQueryListMethods(value: object): value is MediaQueryList {
  58 |   return "addListener" in value && "removeListener" in value;
  59 | }
  60 | 
  61 | // Makes every max-width media query match, so the app lays out as on a phone.
  62 | export function mockPhoneViewport() {
  63 |   vi.spyOn(window, "matchMedia").mockImplementation((query: string) => {
  64 |     const list: Pick<
  65 |       MediaQueryList,
  66 |       | "matches"
  67 |       | "media"
  68 |       | "onchange"
  69 |       | "addEventListener"
  70 |       | "removeEventListener"
  71 |       | "dispatchEvent"
  72 |     > = {
  73 |       matches: query.includes("max-width"),
  74 |       media: query,
  75 |       onchange: null,
  76 |       addEventListener: () => {},
  77 |       removeEventListener: () => {},
  78 |       dispatchEvent: () => true,
  79 |     };
  80 | 
  81 |     Object.defineProperties(list, {
  82 |       addListener: { value: () => {} },
  83 |       removeListener: { value: () => {} },
  84 |     });
  85 | 
  86 |     if (!hasLegacyMediaQueryListMethods(list)) {
  87 |       throw new Error("Failed to construct MediaQueryList mock");
  88 |     }
  89 | 
  90 |     return list;
  91 |   });
  92 | }
```

 306 | import {useCreateAppointmentMutation} from "../queries";
 307 | 
 308 | const appointmentSchema = z.object({
 309 |   patientId: z.uuid("Invalid patient ID"),
 310 |   clinicId: z.string().min(1, "Clinic is required"),
 311 |   doctorId: z.uuid("Invalid doctor ID").nullable(),
 312 |   scheduledAt: z
 313 |     .string()
 314 |     .min(1, "Scheduled time is required")
 315 |     .refine((v) => !Number.isNaN(new Date(v).getTime()), "Invalid date"),
 316 |   durationMinutes: z
 317 |     .number({ error: "Duration is required" })
 318 |     .int()
 319 |     .min(5, "At least 5 minutes")
 320 |     .max(240, "At most 240 minutes"),
 321 |   reason: z.string().max(1000, "Reason is too long"),
 322 |   notes: z.string().max(5000, "Notes are too long"),
 323 | });
 324 | 
 325 | type AppointmentFormValues = z.infer<typeof appointmentSchema>;
 326 | 
 327 | function nowLocalInput(offsetMinutes = 0): string {
 328 |   const d = new Date(Date.now() + offsetMinutes * 60_000);
 329 |   // Format the local wall-clock components without UTC conversion.
 330 |   const pad = (n: number) => String(n).padStart(2, "0");
 331 |   return (
 332 |     `${d.getFullYear()}-${pad(d.getMonth() + 1)}-${pad(d.getDate())}` +
 333 |     `T${pad(d.getHours())}:${pad(d.getMinutes())}`
 334 |   );
 335 | }
 336 | 
 337 | interface AppointmentFormProps {
 338 |   patientId?: string;
 339 |   clinicId: string;
 340 |   defaultDoctorId?: string | null;
 341 |   defaultDurationMinutes?: number;
 342 |   inline?: boolean;
 343 |   onSuccess?: (appointment: { id: string }) => void;
